questions.q: What does std::string::find return if the search substring is not present?
questions.explain: find returns the sentinel value std::string::npos (a very large unsigned value) when the search fails, and this should always be checked before using the result as a position.

questions.q: What does std::stringstream let you do that a plain std::string doesn't directly support?
options: Store more characters than a std::string can hold
Extract or insert typed values using the same >> and << stream operators used with std::cin/std::cout
questions.explain: stringstream wraps a string in the standard stream interface, so typed extraction (>>) and formatted insertion (<<) work on it exactly as they do on cin/cout.

questions.q: In the CSV-parsing pattern `std::getline(ss, field, ',')`, what does the third argument do?
options: It sets the maximum number of characters to read
It specifies the delimiter character to read up to, instead of the default newline
It converts the result to a number automatically
questions.explain: getline's third argument overrides the default newline delimiter, letting it read up to (and consume) a comma — the standard trick for splitting CSV fields.

questions.q: If you open a std::ifstream on a file that doesn't exist, what happens by default?
options: The program throws a std::runtime_error immediately
The stream silently enters a failed state; you must check is_open() or the stream's boolean state to detect this
An empty file is created automatically and read as empty
questions.explain: By default, stream operations do not throw on failure to open a file; the stream simply enters a failed state, which is why checking is_open() before reading is essential.

questions.q: Which header must be included to use std::ifstream and std::ofstream?
questions.explain: File stream classes (ifstream, ofstream, fstream) are declared in the <fstream> header, distinct from <sstream> (stringstream) and <iostream> (cin/cout).
